In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
non-Abelian open strings are not the only way to obtain open string dynamics.

the open strings in the original dual resonance constructions are the same as those in critical closed string theory, but that the D-brane constructions have a different set of boundary conditions, and hence a different open string dynamics.
there is no string theory dual to QCD, at least not in the conventional sense of the word.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the non-Abelian gauge symmetry of D-branes is the key to understanding the gauge theory duals for QCD.
we have found new duals for large N Yang-Mills theory, which have the same massless spectrum as the original duals but differ in their massive spectrum, and in the open string dynamics.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the D-brane construction of gauge theories is a more general and powerful concept than previously appreciated.

the open string dynamics of the original dual resonance constructions are not fully captured by the D-branes in critical closed string theory, which is the main reason why the latter are unable to reproduce the original dual resonance results.
there are many more ways to construct non-Abelian gauge theories with open string degrees of freedom than was previously believed.
